chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One who recites the Surah of Prostration (Sajdah) every Friday night, Allah will give him his book of deeds in his right hand, and He will not call him to account for what he had done, and he will be among the companions of Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: The Ahl al-Bayt (Family of the Prophet), referring to his purified household
key_terms.رُفَقَاءِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Companions of Muhammad, indicating close association and spiritual kinship
key_terms.سُورَةَ السَّجْدَةِ: Surah Al-Sajdah (The Prostration), the 32nd chapter of the Quran
key_terms.كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ: His book (of deeds) in his right hand, indicating ease of reckoning and high status
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ جُمُعَةٍ: Friday night, the night preceding the day of Jumu'ah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Sajdah on Friday night?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) is regarded as the 'Eid of the Ahl al-Bayt,' making this specific night a pivotal time for spiritual preparation. Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes that reciting Surah Al-Sajdah, with its profound emphasis on prostration and divine sovereignty, secures the reward of receiving one's book in the right hand and exemption from harsh reckoning, linking the reciter intimately to the Prophet and his Household.
